CLASS 24 · AGES 4–5 · 32 SPOTTER-CARD LESSONS

Transportation & Vehicles.

HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Thirty-two spotter cards, four vehicles each, one spotting habit.

Every card in this class is a spotter sheet: a group heading — Land, Water, Air or Construction Vehicles — over four labeled vehicles, and every step-by-step lesson right here teaching all four. The order is deliberate: the rides your child already takes come first (car, bus, train, bicycle), then the helper trucks that keep a town running, the rails and the long giants, the boats, the flyers and eleven sheets of construction giants from road roller to tower crane. Each lesson ends with one spotting idea — a hunt, a count, a sort — that carries the words out to real traffic.

Class 24 has been reserved since the school opened; the owner assigned it to Transportation & Vehicles, so the learning path now runs from Class 1 to Class 37 with no gap. One card a sitting is plenty — the whole class is a term of five-minute spotting visits, and the words go with the art: every vehicle named in a lesson is printed on its card.

WHY VEHICLES MATTER

Things that go, thinking that grows.

Vehicles are the friendliest gateway to reasoning a preschooler meets: every body is the answer to a job. Why is the race car pointy? Speed. Why is the armored vehicle slow? Protection. Why does the bus bend in the middle? Corners. The class teaches the questions, and the questions travel — to spoons, chairs, raincoats and every shaped thing the world hands over next.

And the spotting habit is the quiet engine: a child who hunts buses, tractors and tower cranes from the window is doing observation, classification and counting in one game. By the end, your child has thirty-two spotter cards, one hundred and twenty-eight named vehicles and a street that has become a field trip.

SUPPORTING RESOURCE

Print the vehicles cards.

Every lesson has a matching flashcard in the library: the original spotter art as a printable card with a download button, print size and short notes on the four vehicles it names. When your child owns the everyday rides, the vehicles-and-sounds cards take the theme down to age two, and the community helpers lessons introduce the people who drive the trucks.

Open the Transportation & Vehicles flashcards ↗Back to the Learning Path ↗

Age ranges are a guide, not a test. Start with the rides your child already takes — the age pills on every card mark the everyday vehicles Ages 3+ and the specialist machines Ages 4–5 — and follow their eyes from cars to cranes.

SAFER EVERY JOURNEY

From spotting vehicles to crossing streets.

Class 24 names everything that goes; Class 39 · Staying Safe teaches the street rules that go with it: nine road cards for ages 4–5 — traffic lights, the zebra crossing, stop-look-listen, hold hands near roads, helmets on wheels — all on one page with the rule printed on the card and one practice for the very next walk. Spot the bus, then cross like the card says.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your child has met all 32 cards in Transportation & Vehicles, said each word with you and tried one small activity from the lesson.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello! Today we are learning about Transportation & Vehicles. We have 32 cards, and we will look at them one at a time.”

    How: Sit side by side with the cards in front of you. Keep your voice warm and unhurried, and let your child touch the cards.

  2. Cards 1–10
  3. 02
    Card 1 · Car, Bus, Train & Bicycle

    “Car! Bus! Train! Bicycle! The car drives on the road, the bus carries lots of people, the train runs on its tracks, and the bicycle goes round and round on its wheels. Which one have YOU ridden?”

    How: Play the ride report: "who came here today — by car? by bus? on a bike?" Then spot them live from the window and count: two cars… a bus… a bicycle! Naming the rides your child actually takes makes this the most personal card in the set.

  4. 03
    Card 2 · Truck, Motorcycle, Tractor & Ambulance

    “Truck! Motorcycle! Tractor! Ambulance! The truck hauls heavy things, the motorcycle goes zoom, the tractor pulls on the farm, and the ambulance goes NEE-NOR to help people. What jobs do you see?”

    How: Match each vehicle to its job: "who carries the furniture? who plows the field? who helps at an accident?" Then spot them on the road — trucks are everywhere once you look. The ambulance opens the helpers conversation: it is a truck-sized first-aid kit with a siren.

  5. 04
    Card 3 · Tram, Trolleybus, Rickshaw & Cable Car

    “Tram! Trolleybus! Rickshaw! Cable car! The tram rides on rails in the road, the trolleybus holds a stick up to the wire, the rickshaw carries people through the bazaar, and the cable car flies up the mountain on a rope!”

    How: Watch the wires: which of these four follows a line you can SEE? Tram rails, trolley wires, cable ropes — the city’s tracks are hiding in plain sight. Then the hometown question: which of these have you seen here? Which one would you ride first?

  6. 05
    Card 4 · Fire Engine, Police Car, Tow Truck & Garbage Truck

    “Fire engine! Police car! Tow truck! Garbage truck! The fire engine sprays water on fires, the police car keeps us safe, the tow truck carries the broken cars away, and the garbage truck — CRUNCH — takes the trash. Who are the helpers today?”

    How: Spot-a-helper week: every time one of these four passes, say what job it is doing — "the garbage truck is collecting OUR street’s bins!" Then act it out: a toy fire engine rescues the teddy from the sofa mountain. Helper vehicles are the easiest kindness lesson with wheels on.

  7. 06
    Card 5 · Scooter, Skateboard, Roller Skates & Unicycle

    “Scooter! Skateboard! Roller skates! Unicycle! The scooter kicks along the pavement, the skateboard rolls on four little wheels, the roller skates clip-clop in pairs — and the unicycle has only ONE wheel. Balance, balance, balance!”

    How: Try the family of balance: scoot between two markers, stomp-stomp in boots as "roller skates," and try standing on one leg — the unicycle’s whole secret. Count the wheels of all four: two, four, eight… one! The unicycle’s "one" is the giggle finish.

  8. 07
    Card 6 · Van, Minibus, Limousine & Convertible

    “Van! Minibus! Limousine! Convertible! The van is a box on wheels for packages, the minibus seats a whole team, the limousine is a stretched car — loooong! — and the convertible has no roof. Which one would you ride?”

    How: Sort by "what is it carrying?": the van carries boxes, the minibus carries people, the limousine carries movie stars (pretend), the convertible carries sunshine. Then the design question: WHY is the limousine long? Every vehicle’s shape is the answer to its job.

  9. 08
    Card 7 · Bulldozer, Excavator, Crane & Forklift

    “Bulldozer! Excavator! Crane! Forklift! The bulldozer pushes the dirt — vroom, push! The excavator digs a big hole. The crane lifts things UP HIGH, and the forklift beeps and carries pallets. Dig, lift, build!”

    How: Act out the site: push cushions with a "bulldozer" push, dig with a spoon "excavator," lift teddy high with a rope-and-chair "crane" (grown-up power). Then watch a real site from a safe distance and name what each machine is doing — push, dig, lift, carry. Every site is the same four verbs.

  10. 09
    Card 8 · Horse Cart, Sleigh, Wagon & Handcart

    “Horse cart! Sleigh! Wagon! Handcart! The horse pulls the cart — clip clop! The sleigh slides on snow — swoosh! The wagon rolls on four wheels, and the handcart goes wherever YOU push it. Pull, push, slide!”

    How: Pull a box "wagon" of toys across the room, then push the same load on a "handcart" — which is easier? Why? Then the horse-power question: how did people move things before engines? Answer: animals, slides and muscles — all four are on this card.

  11. 10
    Card 9 · Metro Train, Monorail, Funicular & Steam Locomotive

    “Metro train! Monorail! Funicular! Steam locomotive! The metro runs UNDER the ground, the monorail rides ONE rail up high, the funicular climbs the mountain on a rope — and the steam train goes CHOO CHOO with real smoke!”

    How: Rank them by where they run: under (metro), on one beam (monorail), up (funicular), across (steam train). Then the history pair — the steam locomotive and the metro are both trains, a hundred years apart: what changed? (Smoke out, electricity in.) Trains are the clearest time machine in transport.

  12. 11
    Card 10 · Go-Kart, Dune Buggy, Snowmobile & Quad Bike

    “Go-kart! Dune buggy! Snowmobile! Quad bike! The go-kart zips round the track, the dune buggy jumps the sand, the snowmobile slides on snow — vrrroom — and the quad bike goes anywhere its four big wheels can grip!”

    How: Sort by ground: sand buggy, snow sled, track kart, trail quad — each vehicle matches its playground. Then the wheels question: why are the snowmobile’s wheels GONE? (Runners slide where wheels sink.) Adventure machines are shape-follows-terrain, on four very different floors.

  13. Cards 11–20
  14. 12
    Card 11 · Tractor, Combine Harvester, Road Train & Articulated Bus

    “Tractor! Combine harvester! Road train! Articulated bus! The tractor pulls the plow, the combine eats the wheat — chomp chomp — the road train is a truck with THREE trailers, and the articulated bus bends in the middle! Long, longer, LONGEST!”

    How: Order them by length — then the bend question: how does a bus that long turn a corner? (It bends!) Fold a paper "articulated bus" in half and turn the corner yourself. The road train is also a geography story: it belongs to the huge empty roads of Australia, where one truck does the work of three.

  15. 13
    Card 12 · Coach Bus, School Bus, Double-Decker Bus & Electric Bus

    “Coach bus! School bus! Double-decker! Electric bus! The coach goes far away, the school bus brings us to school, the double-decker has TWO floors — climb the stairs! — and the electric bus goes shhh, no engine roar!”

    How: Ride-the-bus pretend: line up chairs, punch paper tickets, ring the bell — "stop please!" Then the counting game: how many wheels does a double-decker need? (Six!) And which bus is the quietest? The electric one hums like a fridge with seats.

  16. 14
    Card 13 · Race Car, Rally Car, Go-Kart Trailer & Armored Vehicle

    “Race car! Rally car! Go-kart trailer! Armored vehicle! The race car goes FAST round and round, the rally car jumps the bumps on gravel roads, the trailer carries the little go-kart — and the armored vehicle is a car in a suit of armor. Strong and steady!”

    How: Race pretend: count down 3-2-1 and "drive" cushions round a rug track, then swap to the slow safe game — the armored vehicle moves slowly because it is protected, not quick. Fast and strong are two different superpowers; this card has both.

  17. 15
    Card 14 · Boat, Ship, Sailboat & Submarine

    “Boat! Ship! Sailboat! Submarine! The boat floats on top, the ship carries the cargo, the sailboat catches the wind — whoosh — and the submarine goes DOWN, down, under the sea! Glub glub glub.”

    How: Float-and-sink lab in the bath: which toys float like the boat, which sink like the submarine? Then the wind test: blow a paper sailboat across the water — wind power, just like the sailboat. And the submarine dive: duck the toy under, periscope up!

  18. 16
    Card 15 · Ferry, Kayak, Canoe & Speedboat

    “Ferry! Kayak! Canoe! Speedboat! The ferry goes back and forth, back and forth, all day. The kayak paddles with TWO blades — splash, splash! The canoe paddles on one side, then the other. And the speedboat goes ZOOM across the bay!”

    How: Paddle practice in a chair-boat: a double "kayak" paddle on both sides, then a single "canoe" paddle swapped left-right — discover why one-sided paddling spins you in circles! Then the ferry question: what goes back and forth across the same water all day? The patient workhorse of the water.

  19. 17
    Card 16 · Yacht, Catamaran, Cruise Ship & Lifeboat

    “Yacht! Catamaran! Cruise ship! Lifeboat! The yacht glides on the wind, the catamaran has TWO hulls — one, two! — the cruise ship is a whole town that floats, and the lifeboat rushes out to help ships in trouble. What a fleet!”

    How: Count the hulls: one on the yacht, TWO on the catamaran — build a "catamaran" from two cups taped together and float it: steadier or wobblier? Then the hero story: the lifeboat crews who launch in storms to save others. Boats have jobs, and the bravest job on the water wears orange.

  20. 18
    Card 17 · Tugboat, Dredger, Hydrofoil & Paddle Steamer

    “Tugboat! Dredger! Hydrofoil! Paddle steamer! The tiny tugboat PUSHES the giant ship — toot toot! The dredger sucks mud like a vacuum. The hydrofoil rises up on wings and flies over the water! And the paddle steamer goes round and round with its paddle wheels — the oldest dance on the river.”

    How: Tug test: can a small toy push a big book across the table? (Slowly… yes — that is a tugboat’s whole job.) Then the hydrofoil question: why would a boat want to LIFT out of the water? (Less splash, more speed.) Harbor boats are the riddle cards of the water set.

  21. 19
    Card 18 · Airplane, Helicopter, Hot-Air Balloon & Rocket

    “Airplane! Helicopter! Hot-air balloon! Rocket! The airplane flies with wings, the helicopter goes whir-whir-whir on top, the balloon floats like a giant bubble — and the rocket goes 5-4-3-2-1, BLAST OFF, all the way to space!”

    How: Fly the fleet: paper-plane "airplane," spinning hand "helicopter," a balloon (real or drawn) drifting up — and the countdown: five, four, three, two, one… BLAST OFF, arms up! Then spot them live: contrails for airplanes, whirring for helicopters.

  22. 20
    Card 19 · Jet, Seaplane, Glider & Blimp

    “Jet! Seaplane! Glider! Blimp! The jet goes faster than sound — WHOOSH! The seaplane lands on the water — splash, gently. The glider rides the wind with no engine — shhh, quiet flying. And the blimp drifts along, slow and round, like a giant fish in the sky!”

    How: Glide test: throw a paper "glider" with the engine off — how far can silence travel? Then the landing question: where does a seaplane park? (On the lake — no runway needed!) And the blimp riddle: why is it so slow? (It floats; it is in no hurry. Some flying is just floating.)

  23. 21
    Card 20 · Drone, Fighter Jet, Cargo Plane & Passenger Plane

    “Drone! Fighter jet! Cargo plane! Passenger plane! The drone hovers and takes photos from the sky, the fighter jet zooms like an arrow, the cargo plane carries the mail and the parcels — and the passenger plane takes families on holiday, up above the clouds!”

    How: Drone-and-pilot pretend: one hand "flies" the drone (slow, hovering), the other works the "remote." Then the job sort: who carries people? who carries boxes? who flies itself? Today’s sky is a workplace — and this card is its staff photo.

  24. Cards 21–30
  25. 22
    Card 21 · Space Shuttle, Hang Glider, Gyrocopter & Flying Boat

    “Space shuttle! Hang glider! Gyrocopter! Flying boat! The shuttle flies to SPACE and back, the hang glider soars slow like a big bird, the gyrocopter’s top blade spins in the wind — whirr — and the flying boat lands on the lake like a duck. Specialists of the sky!”

    How: Hang-glider arms: lean, arms wide, catch the invisible wind, glide across the room — slowest race ever. Then the spaceship question: which one on this card has been to SPACE? (The shuttle — and it landed like an airplane, gliding home.) Sky specialists each solve one problem: space, silence, smallness, water.

  26. 23
    Card 22 · Road Roller, Mixer, Dump Truck & Paver

    “Road roller! Mixer! Dump truck! Paver! The roller goes sllloooow and FLAT, the mixer spins round and round, the dump truck tips its load — crash — and the paver lays the road, smooth like icing on a cake!”

    How: Road-building pretend: a paint roller is the road roller (slow… flat…), a jar spins the "mixing" drum, a toy truck tips the "gravel," and a rectangle block becomes the paver laying the road. Four toys, one finished road. Then spot the real crew flattening a street near you.

  27. 24
    Card 23 · Wheel Loader, Backhoe, Grader & Skid-Steer

    “Wheel loader! Backhoe! Grader! Skid-steer! The loader scoops — CHOMP — a big bite of dirt! The backhoe digs with its back arm. The grader shaves the ground smooth, and the skid-steer — the little one! — turns on one spot like a dancer.”

    How: Scoop relay: move "gravel" (pom-poms) with a toy scoop or a dustpan-loader from pile to bucket — loader style, big bites. Then the spin test: hop on one foot and turn in a circle — a skid-steer pivot! Four machines, one skill: the perfect scoop.

  28. 25
    Card 24 · Drilling Rig, Pile Driver, Telehandler & Boom Lift

    “Drilling rig! Pile driver! Telehandler! Boom lift! The rig drills down, down, DOWN into the ground. The pile driver goes BAM, BAM — giant hammer! The telehandler stretches its arm like a telescope — out and UP! And the boom lift lifts people in a basket, higher than the trees!”

    How: Reach game: how high can YOUR telehandler reach? Stack, stretch, stand on tiptoe (safely!) — then compare with the machine: its "tiptoes" reach six houses high. And the BAM question: why hammer giant nails into the ground? Because tall buildings need strong grips on the earth.

  29. 26
    Card 25 · Scissor Lift, Material Lift, Tunnel Borer & Trencher

    “Scissor lift! Material lift! Tunnel borer! Trencher! The scissor lift goes up like folding scissors — up, up, up! The tunnel borer eats through the mountain — crunch, crunch — a tunnel! And the trencher cuts a long straight line in the ground, like drawing with a giant pencil.”

    How: Scissor-fingers: open and close your hands like the lifting scissors — up they go! Then the tunnel game: crawl through a blanket "mountain" while a partner chants "crunch, crunch, keep boring!" Underground construction is invisible in real life — this card makes it edible.

  30. 27
    Card 26 · Pump Truck, Water Truck, Lowboy & Batching Plant

    “Pump truck! Water truck! Lowboy! Batching plant! The pump truck pours concrete through its long arm — slurp, like a giant straw! The water truck sprays the dust — sprinkle sprinkle. The lowboy carries the BIG machines on its flat back, and the batching plant mixes the concrete right there on the spot!”

    How: Straw engineering: sip a drink through a long bendy straw — that is the pump truck’s whole trick, moving liquid concrete along a folding arm. Then the sprinkle test: a spray bottle "water truck" tames the dusty dirt in the sandbox. Every hero machine needs a support crew — this is theirs.

  31. 28
    Card 27 · Street Sweeper, Snowplow, Line Painter & Rail Grinder

    “Street sweeper! Snowplow! Line painter! Rail grinder! The sweeper brushes, brush brush brush. The snowplow pushes the snow — whoosh, mountains of white! The line painter draws the road’s long yellow lines, and the rail grinder makes SPARKS on the tracks — the road’s tidy-up crew!”

    How: Line-painting pretend: lay masking-tape roads and let your child paint the "yellow lines" with chalk or a brush — straight lines are a real skill the machine does at walking pace. Then the sparks question: why does the rail grinder make fireworks? Grinding metal makes sparks — the train track gets a shave.

  32. 29
    Card 28 · Cold Planer, Asphalt Recycler, Curb Machine & Slipform Paver

    “Cold planer! Recycler! Curb machine! Slipform paver! The planer shaves the old bumpy road — scrape, like a giant cheese grater! The recycler melts the old bits into NEW road. The curb machine squeezes out the sidewalk’s edge, and the paver glides along leaving fresh smooth road behind it!”

    How: Grater demo (grown-up hands): grate a old crayon stub into shavings — that is the planer’s job, chewing off the old surface. Then the recycle idea: old road is not rubbish — it melts and comes back as new road. Roads can be born again!

  33. 30
    Card 29 · Articulated Hauler, Motor Scraper, Pipe Layer & Trench Compactor

    “Hauler! Motor scraper! Pipe layer! Compactor! The hauler bends in the middle — clunk — and carries a whole mountain of dirt! The scraper shaves the ground flat. The pipe layer LAYS THE PIPES in the ground — the water’s secret roads! — and the compactor stamps, stamp, stamps the earth hard.”

    How: Bendy-hauler craft: tape two toy trucks together with a paper hinge — it bends like the real articulated hauler. Then the underground question: where does the tap water come from? Pipes! And the compactor game: stamp the sandbox earth with both feet — firm ground holds roads up.

  34. 31
    Card 30 · Vacuum Excavator, Crawler Carrier, Tracked Carrier & Material Handler

    “Vacuum excavator! Crawler carrier! Tracked carrier! Material handler! The vacuum sucks the dirt — SCHLOOP — no shovel needed! The crawler WALKS on its tank feet — step step step over the mud. And the material handler has a claw — grab, lift, place! Like the biggest claw machine in the world.”

    How: Claw machine pretend: a clothes-peg "grabber" picks up pom-poms and places them on a tower — grab, lift, place, exactly the handler’s verb set. Then the tracks question: why TANK FEET instead of wheels? On soft mud, wheels sink; treads walk. Nature thought of it first — snowshoes!

  35. Cards 31–32
  36. 32
    Card 31 · Tower Crane, Crawler Crane, Rough-Terrain Crane & Truck Crane

    “Tower crane! Crawler crane! Rough-terrain crane! Truck crane! The tower crane is the TALLEST — it watches over the whole city! The crawler walks on treads and lifts the heaviest things. The rough-terrain crane climbs the mud, and the truck crane drives itself to little jobs. Lift, lift, lift!”

    How: Crane height sort: which one is tallest? (Tower crane — its top is often higher than the building it builds!) Then the balance game: hold a book at arm’s length — heavy, right? Cranes do that all day with a counterweight on the other side. Build a spoon crane: spoon arm, cup counterweight, lift a pom-pom load.

  37. 33
    Card 32 · Generator, Light Tower, Compressor & Welding Truck

    “Generator! Light tower! Compressor! Welding truck! The generator makes the electricity — hummm. The light tower lifts its lamps — the site glows at night! The compressor squeezes air for the tools — psshhh. And the welding truck joins the steel with sparks — bzzzz, fireworks at work!”

    How: Night-shift pretend: a torch on a chair is the light tower — the whole site glows. Then the sound hunt: the generator HUMS, the compressor PSHHH-es, the welder buzzes — the site has a soundtrack. And the big idea: before the builders build, someone brings the power.

  38. 34
    Practice

    “Now you are the teacher! Pick any card and tell me what it is.”

    How: Let your child choose the card and say the word in their own way. Teaching someone else is the strongest way to remember.

  39. 35
    Check

    “Can you find Car, Bus, Train & Bicycle? Now show me Tugboat, Dredger, Hydrofoil & Paddle Steamer.”

    How: A point, a fetch or the word all count as a pass. If they are unsure, name it for them and try again another day — there are no scores and no pressure.

  40. 36
    Well done

    “Well done! Today we met 32 cards. Let us look for one of them at home.”

    How: End on a win, then spot one of the words in real life today. Meeting it again in the real world is what makes it stay.

Read the script while you show the cards — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines are the activity behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.
